items.title: 10 Great Video Games That Come Close to Perfection
items.summary: Spectacular titles like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Mass Effect 3 come as close to genuine perfection as a video game possibly can.
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware Add Collider on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Lucas Kloberdanz-Dyck Published Nov 11, 2026, 12:35 PM EST Lucas Kloberdanz-Dyck is a writer for Collider. He grew up creating lists, stories, and worlds, which led to his love of anime and video games. He attended Sheridan College where he earned an Honours Bachelor of Game Design. Lucas and his group won 1st place for technical innovation at LevelUp Toronto 2023, and he was also an intern for the Oakville Film Festival of Arts. Sign in to your Collider account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap In this day and age, everything needs to be perfect in order to get any recognition, leaving the solid 7/10s being regarded as disappointments. This way of thinking is especially true with video games , with only a select few being considered truly perfect, such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Portal 2 .

However, the opposite is also true, with some fans ignoring the flaws of renowned masterpieces. That is why this list will feature 10 video games that come close to perfection but don't quite achieve it . Based on aspects such as minor, yet noticeable flaws, narrative, design, gameplay, visuals, fan opinion, and overall quality, these games came so close to being flawless.

Image via CD Projekt Some of the best video games are being turned into TV shows, such as The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , but the adaptations are rarely as good as the games. Geralt of Rivia is a Witcher, but he must put aside his usual monster-hunting gig in order to rescue his adoptive daughter, Ciri, from the titular spectral hunters that wish to use her powers for evil.

The Witcher 3 is known for its incredible worldbuilding and side quests that immerse characters in spontaneous adventures and subtle lore drops. As good as it is, this game isn't perfect, with many fans having an issue with the repetitive gameplay loop and some clunky movement, especially on Roach. This combat can get stale after a while , holding it back from being perfect.

Player scanning coral underwater in Subnautica Image via Unknown Worlds Entertainment The ocean is vast and deep, with plenty of potential secrets lying in wait, and that is exactly what Subnautica covers. After crash landing on a planet almost entirely covered in water, the player must explore the region and scavenge the crashed ships for resources. Crafting machines, they have to find a way out, whether that be creating a ship or getting rescued.

Subnautica is an underrated adventure video game with one of the greatest open worlds, allowing players to dive into the unknown and learn its secrets. Unfortunately, its ambition was too great for the limited technical capabilities , resulting in frame drops, rendering errors, and overall poor performance in certain areas. Thankfully, the sequel will fix these issues.

super-mario-sunshine.jpg Image via Nintendo Nintendo is one of the greatest video game companies of all time, and while they usually take their time to make everything perfect, some games fall between the cracks. Super Mario Sunshine is a 3D platformer that follows the titular plumber on his vacation to Isle Delfino. However, when he is framed for a crime he didn't commit, he must find the real criminal and clear his name.

3D Mario games are usually known for being perfect, but Super Mario Sunshine has a couple of issues that make it one of the worst in its franchise. This game has annoying difficulty spikes that arise from its flawed programming , which includes poor blue coin tracking, unstable physics, and bad collision, proving the technical errors restricted it from being one of the best 3D Mario games.

A woman carrying a gun stands looking upon a huge room as an ominous red mist known as The Hiss distorts and floods the area in the 2019 video game 'Control'. Image via 505 Games The recent release of CONTROL Resonant has fans talking about the series again, including what Control could have done to be perfect. The Federal Bureau of Control is a mysterious organization in the Oldest House, and when Jesse enters it as the new director, she must handle the mysterious phenomena while also trying to find her brother.

The kinetic feel of this video game highlights the power system and how engaging it is , easily manipulable in the surroundings. However, Control is also notoriously confusing , with the shifting world of the Oldest House making it hard to navigate the multi-layered vertical unit, which can also be very disorienting for the players, even if it is a video game that needs more credit .

fire-emblem-engage-all-emblems-line-up.jpg Image via Nintendo As mentioned, Nintendo has plenty of great franchises, including the cult classic that is Fire Emblem . While the newest entry is already a Game of the Year candidate, its predecessor, Fire Emblem: Engage , was incredibly polarizing. When the Divine Dragon awakens after a thousand years, it must collect 12 emblem rings to defeat the evil Fell Dragon Sombron.

Fans of Fire Emblem: Engage have stated that the gameplay is arguably the best in the entire franchise , making it an infectiously addictive video game — not to mention a bit of fan service done right. However, it is also notorious for its underwhelming narrative , an aspect the overall franchise is known for. Fire Emblem: Engage can be campy and corny at times, not to mention its paper-thin protagonists.

Alien: Isolation video game Image via Creative Assembly It is rare for a movie franchise to turn into a good video game, but Alien: Isolation has proven that it can be done. Amanda travels to a decommissioned space station in order to learn the truth behind her mother's disappearance. However, all she uncovers is a Xenomorph that hunts her down, forcing her to try to escape the haunted space station.

IGN infamously gave Alien: Isolation a bad score, and while it is much better than that, the game isn't perfect. The recently announced Alien: Isolation sequel has plenty of fans excited because it can fix the mistakes of the long playtime and become truly perfect. The narrative padding in the second half extends the game longer than it needs to be, creating a flaw in an otherwise perfect game.

items.title: Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between Manga Ends in Next Chapter
items.content:
Haruichi 's Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between ( Elden Ring: Tōki Hazama no Monogatari ) comedy manga , based on Bandai Namco and FromSoftware 's Elden Ring game, announced on October 19 that it will end in its next chapter. The manga did not reveal when that next chapter will debut, and the manga's webpage says the next chapter's scheduled launch is "to be determined."

The manga will end in its third volume, which was slated to ship on December 4.

Yen Press licensed the series, and it describes the story:

Haruichi ( Star Wars: Visions , Star Wars Leia, Princess of Alderaan manga series) debuted the omnibus collection of short stories in July 2024.

FromSoftware launched the original Elden Ring game for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and PC via Steam in February 2022. The game quickly surpassed 12 million units in sales worldwide in March 2022, and had overtaken Call of Duty: Vanguard as the best-selling game in the U.S. in the last 12 months ending in April 2022. The game's DLC expansion Shadow of the Erdtree launched in June 2024 for PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam . The base Elden Ring game is required for the expansion. The DLC crossed 5 million copies in sales within its first three days of launch.

The game received a version for Nintendo Switch 2 titled Elden Ring : Tarnished Edition that released on August 28, delayed from its 2025 release. The Switch 2 version includes content from the DLC expansion Shadow of the Erdtree . The game also features new armor and a new customization for Torrent's appearance.

Hidetaka Miyazaki ( Dark Souls , Dark Souls III , Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice ) and author George R. R. Martin ( Game of Thrones ) collaborated in creating the original Elden Ring game's world.

The game is inspiring a live-action Hollywood film adaptation that will premiere on March 3, 2028.

items.title: Elden Ring: Path Of Shadows Officially Announced For December 1
items.summary: Elden Ring: Path of Shadows takes Tarnished back through the Abyssal Woods.
items.content:
Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Nicholas Becher Published Nov 11, 2026, 12:00 AM EST Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Most-played games range from Clair Obscur to Civ to Elden Ring to Halo 2 and beyond. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Elden Ring fans are still keeping their fingers crossed for a major announcement regarding the franchise's future. While it's exciting that the A24 film from Alex Garland is on the horizon, Tarnished are still unsure about whether there will be an actual Elden Ring 2 at any point in the future.

Fortunately, thanks to the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 and its accompanying DLC, gamers have every reason to dive back into the Lands Between for another play-through. The Tarnished Edition officially launched on August 28, marking the franchise's long-awaited debut on a Nintendo console. Along with the base game, the release included 2024's massively successful Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, giving newcomers the opportunity to experience the complete adventure in one package.

Now, to close out the year in grand fashion, Elden Ring is returning on December 1 with the official launch of Path of Shadows , taking players back to the Shadow Realm and the dreaded Abyssal Woods for a final tumultuous journey.

Close Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree Land of Shadow. Custom image by Katarina Cimbaljevic Image of Midra Lord Of Frenzied Flame boss in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1840870411"] = '" Close Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree Land of Shadow. Custom image by Katarina Cimbaljevic Image of Midra Lord Of Frenzied Flame boss in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. "'; Bandai Namco is closing out 2026 with Path of Shadows , the fourth and final installment in its ongoing Elden Ring Community Quests initiative. Running from December 1 through December 28, the event challenges players to return to Shadow of the Erdtree and work together toward several ambitious goals, including revisiting some of the expansion's most memorable locations.

Unlike a traditional DLC questline, Path of Shadows is a community-wide event, meaning individual players contribute toward shared objectives rather than completing every challenge themselves. Bandai Namco has outlined five specific goals for the December event:

Fortunately, participation is straightforward. Players simply need to play Elden Ring on their preferred platform during the event, with progress updates and reminders available through the game's official Discord server.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree Messmer key art. As for rewards, Bandai Namco has confirmed exclusive commemorative artwork by Crisppyboat, alongside a special St. Trina Twitch chat badge designed by Carsondrewit. For anyone unfamiliar, Twitch badges are small icons displayed beside usernames in livestream chats, allowing viewers to showcase achievements, affiliations, and other distinctions.

Path of Shadows follows three earlier community quests, each celebrating a different aspect of FromSoftware's acclaimed RPG. The first, Path of the Tarnished , ran from September 1–28, challenging players to summon Sorcerer Rogier and collect various items. Rewards included artwork by Shimhaq and a Sorcerer Rogier Twitch badge.

October's Path of the Cardinal Sin resulted in commemorative artwork by Dan Mumford and a Festering Bloody Finger badge, while November's Path of the Elden Lord , running November 2–28, will feature artwork by Louis Gibiard and a Warrior Jar Alexander badge. All three badges were designed by Carsondrewit.

Bandai Namco is also hosting a separate Discord emote contest, giving artistic fans another opportunity to participate in the celebrations. With Path of Shadows bringing the festivities to a close, there's no better excuse for Tarnished to revisit the Shadow Realm in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree before the year is out.

items.title: How to Beat Malenia in Elden Ring: Best Builds and Summons
10 Long Open World Games That Take Forever to Complete
items.summary: Open-world games like Elden Ring will keep players busy with hundreds of hours of content.
items.content:
Image via FromSoftware Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Sage Ashford Published Nov 7, 2026, 11:15 PM EST Staff Writer for CBR, Sage Ashford has also written for Comicon as well as other sites such as The Gamer, and has been doing freelance work since 2014, and been working for CBR since 2016. His focus is primarily on spreading the word on obscure anime, comic books, and games whenever possible. Follow him on Twitter @ sageshinigami, or on YouTube @ nolevelcap. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Open-world games have dominated gaming in recent years, and a huge part of what makes them so appealing is that they're typically packed with content. The best open-world games are filled with things to do, and in some cases, it'll take hundreds of hours for players to experience everything they have to offer.

Games like Crimson Desert feel endless, and new content updates keep making them bigger. Few games offer more bang for their buck than these ones, and while these games are absolutely bursting with content, they never feel bloated and are worth competing.

A wide shot of a town in the Kingdoms of Amalur world, just before the main character appears Image via THQ Nordic It's rare to get an open-world RPG like Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning . It's a beautiful world with art design that's been unmatched over a decade after its release, meaning anyone could play it today, even if it was viewed as a flop when it released. It's a blast to play, but it's also a title that anyone even remotely thinking of completing everything will be playing for several dozen hours.

Each of the game's massive open zones offers dozens of quests, meaning players will be going through them for hours. That's without considering the different factions the player can join in the world, which all have their own separate faction questlines. Even when all that's done, there are still several DLCs and an expansion to get through.

Rip Mystery Packs of Graded Cards & Collectibles

Japanese Pokémon Center 20th Anniversary Promo · PSA 10

Must be 18+/19+ to participate depending on jurisdiction.

Geralt of Rivia riding on horseback in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt across the landscape of Skellige. Image via CD Projekt Red The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was one of the best games of the PS4 generation. The game set players loose onto a vast, war-torn land, where players split their time between fighting monsters and searching for Geralt's daughter. Even now, the game represents a standard that most games cannot match, a decade later.

The game's main story alone lasts dozens of hours, as players travel across two separate continents for their job. However, there's a vast number of monsters Geralt can help the people with, not to mention the political jobs one can do. Even the game's second DLC, Blood and Wine , is big enough to be a game unto itself, taking players to an entirely new land and offering over twenty hours of new content.

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Image via FromSoftware FromSoftware dominated the early part of the 2020s with Elden Ring . They finally took their classic formula and made it open-world, and set players loose in a massive world with secrets seemingly around every corner. The game turned into a sensation both in sales and on streaming, as everyone tried to test themselves against this challenging RPG.

Part of the reason Elden Ring takes so long to complete is because of its challenge, as even the early game bosses are punishing, demanding players show off some level of mastery of the combat. It's also not a traditional modern open-world game, and players aren't instantly following directions on a map to go everywhere.

Sandrone finally becomes a playable character in Genshin Impact Version Luna VIII, alongside rerunning Citlali in the game's latest 5-Star Wish Banners, as well as offering stunning new costumes. Image via Hoyoverse There might not be a game more suited for gamers in search of endless content than Genshin Impact . Released in 2020, it started out with a vast open world taking place in a single country. Over the years, they've added more countries and more campaigns to extend it's runtime. However, that's only the beginning of what they've done for this game.

Players who get into Genshin Impact can expect plenty of side quests in each new land they visit. Moreover, every character gets their own Character Quests to help develop their stories, even if players haven't yet pulled that character. And that's all without getting into what it takes to help characters reach their max level. Genshin Impact is a title players can lose themselves in for hundreds of hours.

items.title: Alexander, Warrior Jar Artisan Keycap has arrived!

items.content:
Always seeking worthy opponents and new challenges to become the mightiest warrior, Alexander is ready to take his place atop your keyboard. He is the perfect companion for any Tarnished looking to add a little strength, courage, and jar-shaped charm to their setup. Designed as a 1U keycap (20.61x8.757x26.61mm) for R1 placement, Alexander is compatible with MX-style switches. He is made from a high-quality PU resin using a silicon mold and finished with hand-painted details. Product Features:
  • High-quality PU resin construction
  • Silicone- molded with hand-painted details
  • Compatible with MX-style switches
  • Exclusive to the Bandai Namco Store
A warrior through and through, even when the battlefield is on your keyboard. Add Alexander to your collection and let him continue his journey toward becoming a mighty warrior, one keystroke at a time.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.content:
The roar of the Red Lion echoes to the heavens.

He built his might out of love and loyalty, an unstoppable force that bade the stars to halt at the cry of a true champion. And in the Wailing Dunes, the loyalty he shared with others freed him from a fate worse than death. Now, the power of this greatest of Carian generals can rest in the palm of your hand. Standing 12 cm (4.7 in) tall, Starscourge Radahn is stylized figure that features simple articulation, interchangeable left- and right-hand parts that hold his Starscourge Greatsword, his detachable scrawny steed, and a dedicated display stand. Produced with the super-deformed proportions of the FIGURARTS Mini series, Starscourge Radahn is molded from quality PVC and ABS with exact attention to detail paid even at this miniature size. His golden armor, his raging snarl, even the gravity crests on his blades can be made out with perfect clarity. Pre-orders for this charming miniature figure are available now on the Bandai Namco Store. Do not tary, every other limited edition in this series has sold out. *This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

*This products are available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: I Tested Elden Ring On Switch 2 In A Cozy Cafe And It Ran Just Fine, Which Is Great News For A Remarkable Game
items.summary: You shouldn't play it in the rain/but you can play it on a train
items.content:
Elden Ring is an excellent, excellent video game. It’s got that smashy FromSoftware combat, a couple hundred boss fights that are all (mostly) unique and fun, character build customization for miles, a gorgeous and massive open world that’s a treat to explore, an intriguing story and hidden secrets, and a robust DLC that could be a game all its own. There’s a reason (well, many reasons!) why it’s almost universally critically acclaimed and still beloved by fans a few years after launch, too.

I love Elden Ring ! But when Ethan asked me to take on the review of the Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, I wasn’t, like, stoked about it. I beat Elden Ring back when it first came out, easily dumping over 100 hours into the main game and probably another solid 40 or more into the DLC. And I played the Tarnished Edition at a preview event earlier this year for about 20 minutes, after which time I told everyone I spoke with about the experience that yup, that was Elden Ring all right! Elden Ring on a Switch 2! Game’s great, but I don’t necessarily need to play it again. What else is there to say?

It turns out, after playing for review, I do have one additional thing to say: Elden Ring is, apparently, pretty fun to play in public. Ideally at a cozy coffee shop with squoshy chairs where you can purchase hot London fogs to drink while you play.

Elden Ring was technically playable on the go before the Tarnished Edition , for folks with a Steam Deck. I have one of those, but the device, unlike the Switch 2, is not fun to take out in public. It’s heavy to hold, does not have a convenient kickstand, and you have to hold it in your hands to play if you don’t want to drag a controller around too. With the Switch 2, I could set the console on the table with the kickstand out, take the Joy-Cons off, lean back in my chair, and play Elden Ring while soothing cafe music played in the background. Every time I die (which is often), I get a nice sip of tea. I do not rage. I do not tense up. Helpfully, the cat (who is not here in the cafe with me) does not butt her head against the triggers and cause me to swing my sword randomly. Life is good.

In basically every other respect, I stick to my guns from the preview: this is Elden Ring ! It’s on the Switch 2 now! There were concerns after the first round of early previews that it ran poorly, but those were fixed by the time I previewed it earlier this year and remain fixed now. It runs fine. There are still occasional little framerate drops and yeah, it doesn’t look quite as nice as it will on your PS5 or Xbox Series, but who cares? It still plays great. The minor technical compromises didn’t interfere with combat in any way that was meaningful to me. It still looks good. It’s still lovely to stand on a cliff’s edge and look out in the direction of the Erdtree, the sun’s rays glistening through the clouds and a skyline of crumbling ruin all around.

I should mention that the Tarnished Edition does not have any meaningful new features. There are four new armor sets, a bit of customization for Torrent, and two new starting classes. Unfortunately, two of those new armor sets are starting sets for the two new classes, Heavy Knight and Idus Knight. I played as the Idus Knight and replaced my armor almost immediately with some tunic thing I got off a knight in the very first part of Limgrave, because it had better stats. I think I wore this same tunic when I played the game the first time. Shame, because the new starting armor genuinely looked great. I found the addition of these two new classes to be extremely whatever: you’re going to customize all your stats and replace all your gear almost immediately anyway. The Idus Knight was just a Samurai two levels lower, with different equipment. These additions did nothing for me, and certainly will do nothing for anyone after the first hour of game.

This release does include the superb Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, bundled right in from the start, though. That rules.

But who cares? It’s Elden Ring , on Switch 2! I can easily play it on a plane or on a train, in a box or with a fox, here or there, anywhere! I can take it to bars, to rooftop wine parties. I can play it outside on a patio with a cold one in a koozie next to me as the summer sun sets. I recognize that this is just effectively restating the main gimmick of the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but I admittedly haven’t taken my Switch 2 out much since it launched last year. Elden Ring , the best game of 2022 and arguably one of the best games of the decade, is a great excuse to do so. Give it a shot. Order yourself a latte or, a little later in the day, maybe a nice glass of pinot noir, bust out your Switch 2, and give it a shot.

This article was corrected post-publication: Limveld is Nightreign , Limgrave is Elden Ring . I can never keep them straight.

items.title: Elden Ring on the Switch 2 isn’t tarnished
items.summary: An excellent new way to play.
items.content:

The latest version of the open-world epic has me hooked all over again.

Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Senior entertainment editor Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Image: Bandai Namco Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

FromSoftware is hoping to make a splash on the Switch 2 later this year when it launches The Duskbloods , a gothic competitive multiplayer game that’s unlike anything the studio has made before . But before that, Switch 2 owners have a chance to experience the studio’s biggest hit for the first time thanks to a port of Elden Ring and its expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree . For the most part, the new version — called the “Tarnished Edition” — is the same game that captivated players in 2022 . But the shift in platform also makes it a particularly compelling way to explore the Lands Between.

Elden Ring differentiated itself from past FromSoft games by introducing a large open world shrouded in mystery and brimming with danger. And as we’ve learned over the years, open-world games work especially well on Nintendo’s hybrid console, letting you play in small bursts while in portable mode before settling in for grander adventures on your television. Nintendo made this point crystal clear launching the original Switch alongside The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild , and the extra horsepower of the Switch 2 has been put to use for ports of gigantic games like Cyberpunk 2077 .

In many ways Elden Ring is an ideal test case for the Switch 2. It may be a few years old, but it’s a big and demanding game, one where every element matters. Wonky frame rates could mean death in battle, while dark or fuzzy graphics could allow a cave-dwelling creature to get the jump on you. I spent dozens of hours exploring and dying in the PS5 version of the game when it first launched, and I’ve since spent around 10 hours dabbling with the Switch 2 port. And while the Switch 2 edition isn’t the most technically impressive version of the game, it is one that runs just well enough to possibly be my favorite way to play.

Replaying the opening hours of Elden Ring is an interesting experience. It’s easy to forget just how unforgiving the game can be early on. You play as a weak little wretch known as a Tarnished, thrust into an expansive fantasy realm full of things that want to kill you. One of the first things you see is a giant gladiator riding a horse, and if you try to attack it you’ll die from a single swipe of its sword. It’s a powerful learning experience, and much of my time with the Switch 2 version of the game has been spent cowering in bushes and slaying flocks of giant bats in order to slowly level up my fledgling astrologer. I’ve made some progress — I finally took down Margit, the Fell Omen, the game’s first major boss, and I made it to the Roundtable to get a comforting hug from Fia — but mostly I’ve just been puttering around, cautiously poking at the edges of the world, slowly growing in both strength and confidence.

The most important thing about my experience so far is that the limitations of the hardware never had a negative impact. There are some Switch 2 drawbacks, like less detailed characters and some textures that look muddy or washed out. But these are all superficial things, and I found myself largely forgetting about them the more that I explored. I haven’t come across any issues of stuttering or frame rate drops, either in portable or TV mode. Which is all to say that Elden Ring performs well enough on the Switch 2 that, aside from the occasional long load, I haven’t spent much time thinking about the game’s performance at all.

Instead, I’ve found myself once again lost in the Lands Between, spending many of my waking moments reliving adventures or dreaming up where I want to go next. As with other big games on the Switch or its successor, the nature of the platform makes it easier to fit an adventure of this scale into my life. Sometimes, I grab the tablet and just spend 20 minutes clearing out a camp full of soldiers or seeking out the next Site of Grace, making incremental progress that will make life easier when I tuck in to explore for hours in TV mode.

This isn’t a new revelation about the Switch by any stretch. But with Elden Ring ’s sprawling landscape and unforgiving combat, it’s an ideal example of the type for how well this kind of open world can work on the Switch 2. And with The Duskbloods lurking in the shadows , it’s a great way to scratch that FromSoft itch while waiting for the studio’s next game.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition launches on the Nintendo Switch 2 on August 28th.

items.title: Why Elden Ring Tarnished Edition still made me want to explore it all again
items.summary: The Switch 2 port isn’t perfect, but the masterpiece remains.
items.content:
Despite fears and delays, Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is an excellent way to experience FromSoftware's intimidating yet flexible open world masterpiece, whether you're discovering The Lands Between for the first time or a glutton for punishment back for more.

Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test .

Even though I've already put hundreds of hours into Elden Ring back when it first launched in 2022 as well as the release of its substantial Shadow of the Erdtree expansion in 2024, having the most revolutionary open world game this decade (second only to Nintendo's own Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom) on the Switch 2 was always a tantalising prospect when a complete edition was announced for the console in its original reveal.

Of course, that excitement turned to trepidation when initial reactions to the game's performance and optimisation at last year's Gamescom delayed Elden Ring Tarnished Edition from its original 2025 window. Naturally, it would have been a touch too ironic for this port to be a literally tarnished version compared to other releases, but it would also be in FromSoftware's interest not to make a hash of it, especially when it's partnering with Nintendo for Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods . And now, a year later, just in time for the next edition of Gamescom in Cologne, it's a relief that it's still a joy to journey back to The Lands Between in all its majesty.

While Elden Ring was actually a cross-gen release, the Switch 2 version certainly feels closer to current-gen than last-gen. It may not have the hardware grunt to deliver a smooth 60 fps, but the details, from shadows to foliage or the bright lights emitting from the ever-present Erdtree or the sights of grace, don't feel diminished whether you're playing docked or in handheld mode, while I didn't feel like I was stuck on the loading screen for long whenever I died.

The framerate overall feels stable enough that I can freely roam large stretches of this open world on my spectral horse Torrent, just marvelling at anything that catches my eye without things coming to a judder, or parry an enemy's attack and be able to blame myself rather than the game's performance if I mess up the timing.

But one of the refreshing things about coming back to Elden Ring is just how much of a leap it was for FromSoftware. Whereas other Soulslikes feel like they're still working from Dark Souls 3's design, what I had forgotten is how Elden Ring gives you so many more options than parrying, including just being able to block with your shield and immediately follow up with a powerful staggering counter.

More notable is that depending on the weapon you have, the ZL input changes to a much more diverse set of skills, or you can even change them with Ashes of War items. It gives you a much more flexible way to customise your build to fit your playstyle, while you also have the benefit of just being able to browse YouTube guides to all kinds of broken builds. Even then, if you're still struggling by yourself, you also have the ability to seek out and summon spirits to help you out, and while often they're just acting as a distraction, you can also upgrade their effectiveness while they don't increase a boss's HP like when summoning another player.

It's the same philosophy applied to its open world map, which just keeps expanding and expanding the more you explore, where you really can go in just about any direction you like. Want to take on a brutally tough enemy the moment you step out onto the grassy grandeur of Limgrave? You can, or just ride another way and level up with some more manageable mini dungeons, or find and summon spirits to aid you in battle. Or you might find a chest that whisks you off to the nightmarish rotting hellscape of Caelid that you normally wouldn't reach for another 10 or so hours (even though actually there's nothing stopping you from riding in that direction in a matter of minutes from the start).

If you run into one brick wall, you'll almost certainly find something a little more surmountable elsewhere, or conversely you can also just race ahead to some of the late game areas, including unlocking the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion that takes you to a completely different map. Found a weapon or spell you want to use but realised you invested runes in a different kind of build? Then there's a way to respec too, even if you have to work for it first. But the benefit of being a game that's been out for a few years is that there's no shortage of YouTube guides where you can find the most optimal route or a path to crafting the most broken builds.

Yet despite all the hours I've put into the game before, I also just enjoyed being able to rediscover The Lands Between by myself, taking different routes than I had before, forgetting about something I had discovered by accident the first time. I did nonetheless make use of one of the new starting classes included in Tarnished Edition (which will also be added to other versions as a free update), Knights of Ide, with a sword I feel definitely helped me breeze through my first couple of hours. But old habits die hard, and I was soon back to wielding my beloved Bloodhound's Fang, which had always been by my side until the endgame.

With such a rich lore to its world, especially one that Game of Thrones' George R.R. Martin helped shape, the best way to experience Elden Ring, almost like any old book, is just to take your time and savour every drop of it. Even with its expansive cast of demigods, many whom I still sometimes struggle to keep track of given the similarities of their names – your Godfreys, your Godricks, or your Melinas and Melanias – it's the smaller questlines and their recurring characters that really give the game its charm, from the tragic Millicent to the jolly giant Living Jar Alexander, or that dirtbag Patches, who has appeared in many of FromSoft's games in some guise or another. There's no definitive or right way to play Elden Ring, but you'd be missing out if you were to skip the questline featuring a group of characters that the lads at RKG affectionately refer to as 'Welsh Avengers'.

Tarnished Edition is, however, not without some blemishes. Admittedly, I haven't been able to sink in as many hours exploring every nook and cranny of the port as I did with the original release, but I still encountered moments when the game started dropping frames to the point of a slideshow. Yet on these occasions, I think it must also have been something else buggy happening under the hood, as I also spent time wandering in large open fields fighting multiple enemies, including a flying fire-breathing dragon, without the action grinding to a halt. For the most egregious moments, I simply found quitting out and opening the game again usually rectified matters, so it's more occasional bugginess than inconsistent performance.

The benefit of playing Elden Ring on Switch 2 is of course the portability factor but again there's caveats there too since this will definitely drain your battery faster if you don't have a power bank or plug socket to hand, while exploring the darker sections of the game such as its underground caverns and catacombs is going to be a struggle if you're playing outdoors or with sunlight coming from a train or plane window.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2

items.content:
08/11/26 Pre-order now Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching Aug. 28 on Nintendo Switch 2 The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The “Tarnished,” long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on August 28 .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

items.title: Elden Ring Director Reveals Spiritual Successor Titles Are In Development
items.summary: The master of RPGs is set to strike again
items.content:
Dark Souls and Elden Ring creator Hidetaka Miyazaki appears to be back at it again.

Arguably two of the most era-defining games of all time, Dark Souls and Elden Ring are masterpieces.

Hailing from gargantuan Japanese studio FromSoftware, the RPGs have paved the way for an industry of successful mock-ups, and we've been waiting with bated breath to see what will come next.

Now, it looks like numerous games are in the works at the company, as Miyazaki let slip of 'unnamed' projects in the pipeline, amid a shareholder power struggle.

Back in 2024, hot off the back of the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, FromSoftware parent company Kadokawa Corporation teased that it was working on 26 new games , the large majority of them coming to consoles and PC.

This spurred many people on to believe in an Elden Ring successor.

Now, Miyazaki has followed up on this, commenting on the influence of a new investor group that has trumped the shares of Sony in FromSoftware, but has a history of turning games into microtransaction-heavy revenue streams.

In a statement to Japanese outlet Denfaminico Gamer , the Elden Ring creator said that although he is aware of the ongoing business, he was happy with the creative environment at the studio.

"I’m not saying that there’s no room for improvement, but we can freely make the kind of games we want to make without excessive interference," he said

“I think for both myself and for FromSoftware, the most important thing going forward is to maintain this environment and focus as much as possible on game development.

"[Players] will look forward to both the announced and unannounced titles to come.”

On the 'announced' front, this relates to the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2 action game, The Duskbloods , and Elden Ring's port to the same console.

In fact, there's nothing in the way of console and PC games that we know of.

Previously, Miyazaki has flip-flopped between the future of Elden Ring , first claiming that some lore reveals are being withheld for a sequel, before backtracking and ruling out a follow-up game .

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.
